reason: H0 fuzzes only the JPEG decoder through fuzz_image_decoder and does not directly exercise the broad wuffs_base__pixel_swizzler__swizzle_ycck API. Consequently, it lacks explicit fuzz control over independent plane contents and lengths, dimensions, strides, sampling factors, filter selection, destination pixel format, and AVX2 conversion boundaries implicated by S1.
evidence: H0's sole production entry path is wuffs_jpeg__decoder__initialize followed by fuzz_image_decoder; it never calls wuffs_base__pixel_swizzler__swizzle_ycck directly.

wuffs_base__pixel_swizzler__swizzle_ycck accepts independently variable src0/src1/src2 slices, width0..width3, height0..height3, stride0..stride3, h0..h3, v0..v3, triangle_filter_for_2to1, destination configuration, and scratch_buffer_2k.

wuffs_base__pixel_swizzler__swizzle_ycck selects BGRX/RGBX, box/triangle, and x86 AVX2 implementations based on dst->pixcfg.private_impl.pixfmt.repr, sampling ratios, triangle_filter_for_2to1, and wuffs_base__cpu_arch__have_x86_avx2().

The changed AVX2 converters have a scalar fallback at spans below 32 pixels and SIMD looping for larger spans, including 32-pixel stores and end-dependent n calculation; H0 exposes no explicit boundary protocol for these conditions.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated swizzle_ycck fuzzer that derives all slice lengths, dimensions, strides, h/v factors, triangle_filter_for_2to1, destination formats, and Y/Cb/Cr bytes from fuzz input. Include widths around 31/32/33 and 672 boundaries, valid and invalid buffer relationships, chroma extremes, BGRX/RGBX-family formats, and execution on AVX2-capable configurations; where possible, compare AVX2 results with the corresponding scalar converters.
